Bench: Fakkir Mohamed Ibrahim Kalifulla, Uday Umesh Lalit
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal NO(s).

832 OF 2015  (Arising out of S.L.P.(Crl.) No. 9824/2013)
 HANIF ... APPELLANT(S)
 VERSUS  THE STATE OF UTTARAKHAND ...RESPONDENT(S)
 O R D E R Leave granted.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as the respondent.
On 10.01.2014 when we issued notice in the special leave petition, the notice was confined to the quantum of sentence only.
The appellant herein has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 7/16(1)(A)(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as the Act).
The allegation was that the appellant sold adulterated cow milk.
The test of the seized sample revealed that there was less fat content to the extent of 33%.

The appellant is stated to be a small vendor selling tea,
milk and allied items.
The minimum sentence provided for the offence under the Act is three months.
The trial court has imposed the sentence of six months R.I.

Taking note of the minor nature of the offence committed by the appellant and also the punishment for the offence, without making it as a precedent in any other case, while confirming the conviction and fine we modify the sentence to three months R.I. instead of six months R.I. Fine is stated to have already been deposited by the appellant.
With the above modification of the sentence only, the appeal stands disposed of.
